Commentary publishes short pieces in which scholars comment on populism and populist actors. An opinion, an argument, a way of looking at a question. The editor reviews them. Commentary appears four times a year, and its issues are numbered by year.

## Call for Commentary

Commentary starts with invited pieces. Other scholars are welcome too. Read the guidelines below, then submit your piece through the form. It asks for your details, your piece as a file and a short declaration.

[Open the submission form](https://tally.so/r/jaO0lY){.pv-button .pv-button-big}

If the form does not suit you, email your piece to editor@populiverse.com and copy the declaration below into the message.

## Guidelines

**Who can write.** PhD holders and doctoral candidates, with their affiliation stated. The editor decides what is published.

**What to write.** Your view on a question about populism or populist actors. An opinion, an argument, an approach. No partisan advocacy.

**Length.** Up to 1,500 words. About 1,000 is ideal.

**How to write.** PopuliVerse wants to reach readers beyond universities. So where you can, please use plain words and short sentences.

**Pitch.** Each piece opens with a pitch of 50 to 100 words that says what it argues. It is printed at the top of the piece. Nothing has to be sent beforehand.

**Sources.** You choose the form. Links in the text, author-date references, a reference list at the end, or none. The editor may ask for a source for a factual claim.

**Whose views.** Every piece carries a line saying that the views are the author's own.

**Review.** Pieces are reviewed by the editor. Commentary is not peer-reviewed.

**What you send.** The piece, your affiliation and the short declaration below, through the [submission form](#call-for-commentary). Your ORCID iD is welcome but not required.

**Cost.** None.

**How a piece is published.** As a web page and as a typeset PDF, with its own DOI. It is also collected in the PDF of its issue.

**After publication.** Corrections and the right of reply are set out in the [editorial policy](../about/editorial-policy.qmd).

## The Author's Declaration

The declaration has two parts. In the form, you tick the first and choose one line in the second. If you send your piece by email instead, copy the first line into the message and keep the one line of the second that applies to you.

**1. The piece**

- I confirm that the piece and the views in it are my own, and that I name in it any earlier version and any tie to an actor I discuss.

**2. AI tools**

- were not used
- were used for language only (spelling, grammar, translation)
- were used in drafting. I have checked every sentence and I answer for the text

Pieces are published under CC BY 4.0, so anyone may share and adapt them with credit to the author. If you would rather use CC BY-ND 4.0, which allows sharing but not changes, just say so to the editor.

Sending a piece does not guarantee publication. The editor decides in each case. Authors keep the copyright in their pieces. What the licences allow is on the [licence page](../legal/licence.qmd).
